background: Former Stanford point guard (2005-09) who came up through the Spurs organization: Austin Spurs (G League) assistant and then head coach (2018-19), San Antonio assistant under Gregg Popovich from 2019. Became acting head coach on Nov 2, 2024 when Popovich suffered a stroke, started 8-6 and finished 32-45 (team 34-48; the NBA later formally credited those games to Johnson, resetting Popovich to 1,390-824). Named permanent head coach on May 2, 2025 when Popovich moved to president of basketball operations. In his first full season (2025-26) he led a young Spurs team built around Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and rookies Dylan Harper and Carter Bryant to 62-20, the Southwest title, the 2026 All-Star Game head-coaching assignment, and a run to the NBA Finals (second-round win over Minnesota, Western Conference Finals win over Oklahoma City; Finals opponent/result not verified in this session). Described as calm, process-driven and communicative; credited by Spurs media with 'cracking the Wembanyama code' by pairing tempo and three-point volume with Horns/rip-screen set design.
